spillover_issues.author: ravwojdyla-agent
spillover_issues.body:
## TL;DR

Run a five-day spike to post-train a Snowball specialist for Python problems with executable tests. Start from the pinned September 23 supervised fine-tuning (SFT) checkpoint. Run the coding tasks through `lib/shellbox`, with ShellSim as the first environment backend. Measure coding improvement, export a teacher, and verify its use in multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). A successful integration does not establish a capability gain.

## Description

A coding expert is a specialized Snowball checkpoint. MOPD combines domain teachers by routing student-generated responses to the appropriate teacher for token scores. This spike supplies and validates the coding teacher.

Use [open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-GLM53-RLVR-SFT-2026.09.23](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-GLM53-RLVR-SFT-2026.09.23/tree/227263f32121ac79ba96de6136b86221e58b05db) at revision `227263f32121ac79ba96de6136b86221e58b05db`. This is the latest published Snowball SFT checkpoint found on September 29. It continues the September 21 Datakit SFT model with 5,000 GLM 5.3 conversations and 136 supervised updates. The RLVR term in its name describes the source conversations. Pin its tokenizer and chat template with the weights.

Use this parent for the frozen baseline, coding specialist, and controlled MOPD student experiment. Establish fresh baseline scores. The earlier mixed-RLVR Step92 results do not describe this parent.

The implementation can reuse these components:

- [Curriculum coding SFT](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/871b505121ba2730033e802dd4370825ac0d4ca1/experiments/post_training/curriculum_sft/code_trial.py): task generation, execution checks, verified solution selection, training, export, and evaluation. Its current four-step recipe uses a different parent.
- [Marin RL artifacts](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/871b505121ba2730033e802dd4370825ac0d4ca1/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py): explicit role geometry, model and data dependencies, and HF export. Keep experiment composition in `experiments/post_training/coding_expert*.py`.
- [`lib/shellbox`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/562d705673859548c58b46d8f2383ab8a053797f/lib/shellbox): persistent Harbor shell environments and the external `BashAgent`.
- [Grug TaskCompendium smoke](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9527): the current pinned-HF and Megatron base for this spike. PR #9507 is broader workflow migration work and is not a prerequisite.
- [Snowball MOPD smoke](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/749): four completed updates with three teachers on 64 H100s. That result excludes benchmark improvement and HF conversion validation.

The implementation starts from PR #9527 and pins MarinSkyRL `e26273f7968cf124cc667372b3147da5b6c7a0cf`. This runtime supports the terminal-bench Harbor runner, Megatron training, a ShellSim-aware launch preflight, and explicit custom Harbor agent import paths. The spike pins the parent, tokenizer, Shellbox revision, ShellSim version, task data, and runtime before each run.

Prepare approximately 2,000–5,000 training problems, subject to the source audit. Reserve separate development and final sets before model-based screening. Keep variants of one problem in the same split. Remove benchmark overlap and check overlap with the parent's additional GLM SFT corpus. Record source revisions, problem IDs, verifier settings, and rejected rows. These checks do not establish absence from pretraining.

Materialize each selected problem as a Harbor task package. The task gives the agent a persistent Shellbox Bash session and asks it to write `/workspace/solution.py`. Private tests execute the file against the pinned standard-input or function-call cases. The verifier writes binary reward only after all tests pass. Do not put private tests or expected outputs in the agent-visible environment.

Use `shellbox.backends.shellsim.environment:ShellSimEnvironment` and `shellbox.agent:BashAgent` for the smoke and pilot. ShellSim 0.1.20 provides simulated `python` and `pytest`, so it can run these tasks without a Docker image or network. Run known-pass and known-fail canaries before model rollouts. Harbor uploads private tests only after the agent turn. The custom verifier downloads the submitted program and private cases after that upload, then starts a separate host subprocess and a fresh ShellSim Python process for each case. This keeps the agent session out of the verifier and contains ShellSim child timeouts. Treat the reward as exploratory and recheck the selected candidate on public code evaluations and a clean held-out execution path before a capability claim.

Start with code-only reinforcement learning from the SFT parent. Use the terminal-bench Harbor entrypoint so each rollout can edit files and run tests through Shellbox. Use a short verified-SFT warmup only if the pilot lacks successful solutions or valid tool calls. Initial candidates are 64 prompts per update, four samples per prompt, one update epoch, and learning rate `5e-7`. Bound the run to approximately 20–60 updates and a fixed compute limit. The one-update smoke and pilot measurements determine the final settings before the full training run.

Use binary reward for passing all tests. Record verifier, agent, and infrastructure failures separately from incorrect programs. Measure turn-cap exits, response length, tool-call validity, test failures, and groups that contain different rewards. Earlier mixed-domain Snowball runs lost coding signal through output truncation and constant-zero reward groups ([trace audit](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/507)). The shared SFT trial also records destructive math updates at high learning rates ([results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/871b505121ba2730033e802dd4370825ac0d4ca1/experiments/post_training/curriculum_sft/README.md)). These are reasons for bounded pilots and frequent evaluation.

## Hypothesis or Goal

Short, execution-verified post-training can improve held-out Python correctness and produce a teacher that supplies valid MOPD evidence.

Primary metric: held-out coding pass@1 at a fixed generation budget. Target a gain of at least five percentage points over the frozen SFT parent. Report paired uncertainty across problems. Treat this threshold as a research target, not a forecast.

Supporting evaluations: HumanEval+, MBPP+, and CRUXEval output. Use thinking off and explicit settings from the [September 24 evaluation policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9409). Label shorter internal evaluations separately. Measure MATH-500 and IFBench at the parent, expert, and distilled-student stages to record changes outside coding.

Teacher acceptance requires an HF reload, matching tokenizer fingerprints, finite token scores, and exact alignment with the student's generated tokens. Start with chosen-token evidence and `sampled_reverse_kl` under the [existing OPD contract](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/3b620d8b2bc2ac927d1e4b7004e2d456474e714a/skyrl-train/docs/algorithms/opd.rst).

Add an explicit `code` route. The existing smoke's `swe` route also contains tool-call tasks, so the new expert must not replace that route without a data change. Hold the other teachers fixed. If compute permits, compare matched student updates with the SFT parent versus the new expert as coding teacher. Finite loss proves integration only. A transfer claim requires improved student evaluation results.

A candidate qualifies for teacher integration after a positive held-out pass@1 point estimate and successful teacher acceptance checks. Report gains whose paired interval includes zero as unresolved. The five-point target remains the target for a useful coding expert.

## Status

The source audit is complete. Artifact `2026.09.29.2` accepted 5,567 problems after gold-solution ShellSim preflight and contains 2,400 training, 300 development, and 300 sealed final tasks. Its published runtime bundle includes ShellSim's `_native.abi3.so`. Artifact `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/rav/documents/snowball-python-expert/2026.09.29.3` completed with the first ShellSim-aware MarinSkyRL pin, but its launcher fix read the wrong resolved-config field. Replacement artifact `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/rav/documents/snowball-python-expert/2026.09.29.4` completed in 7 minutes 18 seconds with corrected MarinSkyRL commit `92fbe5126329c38659b54913424e64c39bbeab89`. Its manifest has fingerprint `9dd2b7ad`, and the artifact contains 15,040 staged files. It pins source data, tokenizer, Shellbox commit [`c96bf413`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/c96bf413031fdde2fea1cfd30b4133b44c959a8c), ShellSim 0.1.20, the custom environment, and verifier. The earlier artifacts are superseded for training.

The frozen-parent public evaluation is complete. HumanEval+ pass@1 is 51.83%, MBPP+ pass@1 is 42.06%, CRUXEval input pass@1 is 4.63%, and CRUXEval output pass@1 is 8.88%. The record contains valid aggregate metrics but reports zero graded samples because the archive does not map each task's count field (#9538). Use the canonical aggregate values for the baseline. Do not report sample-level uncertainty from this record.

A direct-verifier smoke produced 10.55% sample reward and 21.88% pass@4, then failed during the first optimizer update because the policy and KL reference filled one 80 GiB H100. That run produced no checkpoint. A lower-memory rerun was canceled after the environment changed to Shellbox. The next gate is one Shellbox Megatron update, checkpoint, HF export, and reload.

The Shellbox path has confirmed runtime gaps and bounded workarounds. The pinned SkyRL image does not include Shellbox or ShellSim (#9532), so the data artifact carries their pinned runtime packages, including ShellSim's native module. The first workaround for custom `BashAgent` selection changed Harbor's shared named-agent map during environment import. Pilot 6 confirmed that this has a concurrent-start race (#9533). MarinSkyRL commit `e26273f79` exposes `AgentConfig.import_path`, rejects a conflicting named agent, and passed all 17 focused builder tests. The recipe now selects `shellbox.agent:BashAgent` through this explicit field. A ShellSim child timeout can terminate its parent trial (#9535), so verification runs in a separate host subprocess. Local metadata can select a missing storage bucket (#9536), so data preparation runs from a CoreWeave coordinator with the mapped S3 prefix. Local graph compilation did not reject a derived Harbor turn limit (#9542), so the recipe now passes the pinned runtime parser before launch. The launcher also treated every terminal-bench run as Daytona (#9543). The first workaround read `skyrl.terminal_bench` and failed again before H100 allocation because the resolved schema uses `skyrl.terminal_bench_config`. Corrected MarinSkyRL commit `92fbe512` uses the resolved field, and all 13 focused preflight tests pass.

Smoke 4 passed launch preflight and allocated five H100×8 nodes. The 32-rank Megatron policy and eight-way vLLM service initialized, all four Harbor rollout workers started, and training entered global step 0. All observed rollout batches then failed 0/4 before generation because `BashAgent` sent Harbor's `hosted_vllm/<model>` alias to the strict vLLM endpoint (#9546). Inspection also confirmed that `BashAgent` did not forward the configured 4,096-token call limit (#9548), and ShellSim could not copy agent logs to the remote S3 target (#9547). The run was canceled after 23 minutes to release 40 H100s. It produced no optimizer update, checkpoint, or export.

Shellbox commits `739c5c052` and `cb4a330d9` normalize direct model requests, forward the LLM call settings, and stage remote log downloads through a local directory. Four focused Shellbox tests, 27 recipe and SkyRL tests, Ruff, Pyrefly, the repository pre-commit checks, and the lint catalog review pass. Artifact `2026.09.29.5` completed in 7 minutes 45 seconds and pins Shellbox `cb4a330d9`. Its remote root contains the train, development, and final splits, runtime packages, artifact metadata, and provenance.

Smoke 5 completed the one-update training and export gate. The 32-rank Megatron policy and eight-way vLLM service initialized on 40 H100s. All five training tasks succeeded in about 19 minutes. Rollout batches completed, including 4/4 batches, and observed task rewards included both zero and one. The optimizer reached `global_step=1` and wrote its checkpoint. The export job then loaded that checkpoint on four H100×8 nodes, wrote 79 Hugging Face safetensor shards, and verified that the shard index references a complete set. The terminal record is `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/rav/checkpoints/snowball-python-expert-smoke/2026.09.29.5/terminal.json`; the policy export is `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/rav/checkpoints/snowball-python-expert-smoke/2026.09.29.5/exports/global_step_1/policy`.

The model also emitted undeclared tool names. `BashAgent` ended those trials instead of letting the model correct its action (#9554). Shellbox commit `ee9e2b9f0` now returns a structured error for an unsupported name and keeps the Bash-only execution boundary. Artifact `2026.09.29.6` completed with fingerprint `2bc9e23d` and this exact pin. Smoke 6 training succeeded at `/rav/snowball-python-expert-shellbox-smoke-6-coord/users-rav-checkpoints-snowball-python-expert-smoke-2026.09.29.6-7492a47bf176`: all five H100×8 tasks completed without a failure or retry in about 19 minutes. Repeated rollout batches completed 4/4, and the run logged both zero rewards and at least 13 reward-one trajectories. Its four-node export also succeeded in about 14 minutes and wrote the expected 79 shards. Commit `1865ae43e` adds a bounded reload stage that serves the real export and runs one evaluation item. Coordinator `/rav/snowball-python-expert-reload-smoke-6-coord` succeeded; its H100×8 evaluation loaded the smoke 6 export in vLLM and served the request. The update, checkpoint, export, and reload gate is complete.

Pilot 6 exposed the shared agent-map race under 32 concurrent trials. At least two trials created Harbor's built-in `OracleAgent` before the custom environment module changed the map. They failed while looking for a benchmark solution script that is not part of these coding tasks. Other trials used `BashAgent`, which confirms inconsistent agent selection in one rollout batch. The pilot was stopped before an optimizer update because it could not produce qualifying evidence. The incident is recorded in #9533. The next gate builds artifact `2026.09.29.7` with MarinSkyRL `e26273f79`, repeats one update with explicit custom-agent selection, and then starts a new four-update pilot only if no Oracle trial appears.

| Day | Planned work | Required output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 — Sep 29 | Pin inputs and runtime. Audit the source. Measure the frozen parent. Confirm reward diversity and runtime faults. | Source audit, parent aggregate scores, direct-smoke evidence, and linked fault reports. |
| 2 — Sep 30 | Build the selected runtime with unsupported-tool recovery. Repeat the one-update smoke and reload its export through vLLM. Validate private-test isolation and known-pass, known-fail, and timeout canaries. | Reviewable spike PR, valid Shellbox traces, checkpoint, HF export, and reload. |
| 3 — Oct 1 | Run bounded coding RL. Apply verified SFT first only if the pilot requires it. Evaluate intermediate checkpoints. | Candidate with a development-set gain, or a documented negative result. |
| 4 — Oct 2 | Freeze the candidate. Run final and supporting evaluations. Export durable HF weights and validate teacher scores. | Evaluated expert artifact with provenance and limitations. |
| 5 — Oct 3 | Run coding-route MOPD acceptance. Do the matched transfer comparison if time permits. Complete checks and the report. | Reproducible PR, expert results, and MOPD integration evidence. |

The schedule assumes accelerator access. The first five-node layout used 40 H100s and failed from policy-plus-reference memory pressure. The Shellbox layout removes the unused KL reference and uses four policy nodes plus one rollout node. Smoke 4 proved that this 40-H100 layout initializes, but it failed at the agent request boundary before generation. Existing MOPD geometries suggest 48 H100s for single-teacher OPD and 64 for three-teacher MOPD. Revalidate each allocation for the selected checkpoint and runtime. The published SFT export reports FP32 tensors, so validate BF16 conversion and serving explicitly.

Smoke 5 used about 12.7 H100-hours for training and 7.5 H100-hours for export, based on the observed 19-minute and 14-minute task durations. Smoke 6 matched those durations. A four-update pilot should use about 58 H100-hours if training time scales linearly and export stays constant. Use the pilot measurement to set the full-run limit. Keep large model artifacts in the same storage region.

Completion criteria:

- [x] Pin parent, tokenizer, data, runtime, verifier, and evaluation settings.
- [x] Register separate training, development, and final problem sets with overlap checks.
- [x] Complete a real update, checkpoint, HF export, and reload on the selected runtime.
- [ ] Report coding results and non-coding changes against the same frozen parent.
- [ ] Preserve the evaluated candidate and its provenance beyond temporary checkpoint expiry, including negative results.
- [ ] Validate coding-route teacher scores and complete a bounded MOPD integration, if a candidate qualifies.
- [ ] Publish the experiment PR, run links, compute use, negative results, and decision in this issue.

A negative result completes the research spike when the evidence explains the failure and records the next decision. It does not satisfy the useful-expert or transfer criteria.
